notes: Eighteen turns, two events, three numbered section headings. The page begins with heading 6, not inside a speech, so opens_mid_utterance is false. Two calls the count depends on, both made under rule 2: the two 'Sr. Presidente.-' labels round each vote are separate turns ('Lo ponemos en consideración.' then, after the votación note, 'Aprobado por unanimidad.'), and under heading 7 the chair is labelled twice in a row with nothing between — 'Aprobado por unanimidad.' and then 'Por favor, senador Zamora.' — which is two turns because two labels are printed, although under heading 6 the same two sentences run on inside a single labelled turn. The oath formula 'Señor senador don Federico Pinedo: ¿juráis a la Patria...' and its twin for Zamora are unlabelled paragraphs continuing the chair's turn, not separate turns and not inserted documents: the chair speaks them. '(Aplausos.)' appears twice, both times inside the chair's paragraph at the end of 'Dios y la Patria os lo demanden.', so under rule 4 it is part of that turn and not an event; I left it out of first_words as it falls after the quoted opening. The two italic '- Se practica la votación.' lines each stand as their own paragraph and are events. The chair is printed with no surname throughout, so I supplied none. Typographic detail: the bold stops before the terminator on most labels ('Sr. Presidente' bold, '.-' roman) but a few are fully bold ('Sr. Pinedo.-', 'Sr. Zamora.-', 'Sr. Presidente.-' at 'Si así no lo hiciereis'); same label either way. Heading 8 uses an ordinal masculine 'º' where headings 6 and 7 have no ordinal. Rozas's turn starts at the foot of the page and runs on.
